name: Vaporwave
aliases: A E S T H E T I C
summary: Pink and cyan gradients, Greek busts, palm trees, Japanese text, 1990s desktop windows and a sunset grid. It came from online music scenes around 2011 and looks at 1980s and 1990s consumer dreams with irony.

philosophy.core_thesis: Nostalgia for a future that did not happen: use the dead gloss of 1990s corporate culture to question it.
design_principles: Set a gradient from magenta (#FF71CE) through violet to cyan (#01CDFE) at 135° across the hero.
Draw a perspective grid floor of 2px lines in cyan or pink with a horizon at 55% to 65% of the viewport height.
Place a classical statue, a palm or a sun disc with horizontal cut-lines (6 to 8 bars) as the focal image.
Show content in retro desktop windows: 2px bevelled border, a 24px title bar and 3 square buttons.
Set headlines in wide-tracked capitals (+0.3em) and add a line of Japanese katakana at 50% of the size.
Use a dark purple ground (#2A1B5C) for text areas and keep body text at 16px with contrast of 7:1 or more.
Add a scanline overlay of 2px stripes at 6% opacity and a glow of 8px to 16px on neon text.
anti_patterns: Neutral flat palettes with no neon
Photographs of real, modern people in daily use
Subtle, serious tone with no irony
Realistic dark mode with grey surfaces

layout.grid_mechanics: A loose layout of windows on a 12-column grid with 24px gutters; windows overlap by 16px to 48px and sit on a perspective floor.
layout.whitespace_ratio: 25% to 35% of the surface stays empty; the spacing scale is 8, 16, 24 and 48px.
layout.alignment_rules: Centred hero and flush-left windows; elements float at slight offsets of 8px to 24px.
layout.container_geometry: Windows with a 0px radius and a 2px outset bevel; neon edges with a 1px glow; sun discs and circles for accent.

font_pairings.note: A wide, techno display face with a monospace text face.
A lower-case mono display for a pure net style.
Roman capitals that echo the statue, with a mono text face.

typography.tracking: Display takes +0.2em to +0.3em; body stays at 0.04em.
hierarchy_rules: Use two weights: regular (400) and bold (700).
Set headlines in upper case with wide tracking.
Add a katakana or full-width text line under each main heading.

color.palette_structure: Neon pink, cyan and violet on deep purple, with one pale mint.
color.contrast_rules: Text on night violet holds at least 7:1; neon colours carry headings, borders and glow, not long text.
color.surface_treatment: Smooth 2-stop or 3-stop gradients for the ground; flat grey for windows; a scanline overlay at 6% opacity.
color.light_and_shadow: A neon glow of 8px to 16px blur around headings and lines; no soft cast shadow.

materiality.surface_simulation: Early graphical desktop: grey bevelled windows and glossy CRT glow.
materiality.border_rules: A 2px outset bevel (white top-left, dark bottom-right) on windows; a 1px neon line on panels.
materiality.blur_and_elevation: Glow of 8px to 16px blur on neon elements only; windows have a 4px hard shadow.

ornamentation_details.iconography: Pixel or bevelled icons at 24px with a solid fill, square terminals and a one-pixel dark edge.
ornamentation_details.illustration: Statues, palms, sun discs, grids and early 3D renders in neon tones; glitch and dither effects at 10% to 20%.

motion.transition_physics: Slow, dreamy drifts and loops: statues rotate 360° in 20s; the grid floor scrolls at 4s per cell; windows fade in over 400ms.
motion.hover_and_active: Hover adds a 12px neon glow and a shift of 2px in the window; active state inverts the colours of the title bar.

emotion.target_response: The viewer feels dreamy, ironic nostalgia for an artificial past.

avoid_when: The audience is conservative, medical or financial.
The page needs a serious, neutral tone.
The product needs fast reading of dense content.

modifiers.how: Replace the neon with soft sky blue and green and glossy bubbles; keep the windows.
Add chrome type, pixel icons and a lighter palette of silver and baby blue.
Replace the bevels with frosted glass panels of 16px blur; keep the gradient.

pack.why: A pixel family from the era of the first desktop windows, with square terminals.
